informal_slogan: For any two Hurwitz quaternions a and b, where b is not zero, there are quaternions q and r such that a equals q times b plus r, and the norm of r is less than the norm of b.
formal_slogan: For any two elements a and b in the Hurwitz quaternions, where b is not zero, there exist elements q and r such that a equals q times b plus r, and the norm of r is strictly less than the norm of b.

informal_slogan: If multiple random variables are independent, the multidistance measure equals the entropy of their sum minus the average of their individual entropies.
formal_slogan: If a list of random variables are independent, the multi-distance measure equals the entropy of their sum minus the average of their individual entropies.

informal_slogan: If X is a submartingale and phi is a convex, continuous, increasing function such that phi applied to each X_t is integrable, then the composition phi(X) is also a submartingale.
formal_slogan: If X is a submartingale and φ is a continuous, convex, and increasing function such that φ(X_t) is integrable for each time t, then the composition φ(X_t) is also a submartingale with respect to the same filtration.

informal_slogan: The projection of a measurable set in the product of two measurable spaces onto the first space is universally measurable, provided the second space is standard Borel.
formal_slogan: The projection of a measurable set in a product space onto the first component is universally measurable, meaning it is null-measurable with respect to any finite measure on the first space. This holds when the second space is a standard Borel space.

informal_slogan: The functor Spec maps Hopf algebras over a ring R to affine group schemes over the spectrum of R, and every affine group scheme over Spec R arises in this way up to isomorphism.
formal_slogan: The functor Spec sends commutative Hopf algebras over a ring R to affine group schemes over the spectrum of R, and every affine group scheme over Spec R arises this way. A group scheme over Spec R is in the essential image of this functor if and only if it is affine.

informal_slogan: If two random variables X and Y are independent and take values in a group G, the Ruzsa distance between them is defined as the entropy of their difference minus half the entropy of X and half the entropy of Y.
formal_slogan: If two random variables X and Y with values in a countable abelian group G are independent, then the Ruzsa distance between them equals the entropy of their difference minus half the entropy of X and half the entropy of Y.

informal_slogan: If two independent random variables take values in a group, then the entropy of their sum or difference is at least as large as the entropy of either variable alone.
formal_slogan: If two independent random variables take values in a countable additive group, the entropy of their sum is at least as large as the maximum of their individual entropies.

informal_slogan: A toric variety over a field k is a scheme X with an action by a torus T, where T is embedded as a dense open subset of X in a way that respects the group action. The torus acts on itself by multiplication, and this action extends to the whole space X. This structure links the geometry of X to the algebraic structure of the torus.
formal_slogan: A toric variety over a field k is a scheme X that contains a torus T as a dense open subset, where the action of T on itself extends to an action on all of X. The torus T is a group scheme that becomes isomorphic to a product of multiplicative groups after base change to a separable closure of k. The structure involves a scheme X over the spectrum…

This result compares how adding independent random variables affects the distance measure…

Specifically, the increase in distance when replacing Y with Y+Z or conditioning on Y+Z is contr…
formal_slogan: If X, Y, Z are random variables in an abelian group, with Y and Z independent, then the difference in Ruzsa distance between X and Y+Z versus X and Y is bounded by half the difference in entropy of Y+Z and Y, which can also be expressed in terms of the Ruzsa distance between Y and Z and the entropies of Y and Z.

informal_slogan: The maximum possible density of sphere packings in 8-dimensional space is achieved by the E8 lattice packing.
formal_slogan: The highest possible density of sphere packings in 8-dimensional space is equal to the density achieved by the E8 lattice arrangement. This density is the supremum of all possible packing densities in that dimension. The value is expressed as an extended nonnegative real number.

informal_slogan: The conditional entropy of two random variables X and Y given a third variable Z equals the sum of the conditional entropy of Y given Z and the conditional entropy of X given both Y and Z.
formal_slogan: The conditional entropy of two random variables X and Y given a third variable Z is equal to the sum of the conditional entropy of Y given Z and the conditional entropy of X given both Y and Z. This rule breaks down the uncertainty of the pair (X, Y) given Z into two parts. It assumes all variables have finite possible values and are measurable.

informal_slogan: If G is a torsion-free group and X, Y are random variables taking values in G, then the distance between X and 2Y is at most 5 times the distance between X and Y.
formal_slogan: If G is a torsion-free abelian group and X, Y are random variables taking values in G with finite ranges, then the distance between X and twice Y is at most 5 times the distance between X and Y, measured with respect to their probability distributions.

informal_slogan: For a tuple of at least two random variables taking values in a group, the sum of the pairwise Ruzsa distances between distinct variables is at most m times (m minus one) times the multidistance of the tuple.
formal_slogan: For a tuple of m random variables taking values in a countable abelian group, the sum of the Ruzsa distances between all distinct pairs is at most m(m-1) times the multidimensional Ruzsa divergence of the tuple.

informal_slogan: Any cadlag local submartingale can be written as the sum of a cadlag local martingale and a predictable, increasing, cadlag, locally integrable process that starts at zero, and this decomposition is unique almost surely.
formal_slogan: Every cadlag local submartingale can be decomposed into the sum of a cadlag local martingale and a predictable, increasing, cadlag process whose supremum is locally integrable.

informal_slogan: If the conditional mutual information between X and Y given Z is zero, then X and Y are conditionally independent given Z, and vice versa. This means that knowing Z, X provides no additional information about Y and Y provides no additional information about X. The result links zero mutual information to conditional independence.
formal_slogan: The conditional mutual information between two random variables X and Y given a third variable Z is zero if and only if X and Y are conditionally independent given Z. This means that knowing Z, the value of X provides no additional information about Y and vice versa. The result holds under standard measurability and finiteness conditions on the va…

informal_slogan: If a stochastic process is progressively measurable and the collection of its values at bounded stopping times is uniformly integrable, then the process belongs to class D.
formal_slogan: If the values of a stochastic process stopped at any bounded stopping time are uniformly integrable, and the process is progressively measurable, then the process is of class D, meaning it is adapted and the collection of its values at all finite stopping times is uniformly integrable.

informal_slogan: The entropy of a random variable that takes values in a group is the same as the entropy of its negation. This means flipping the sign of the variable does not change its uncertainty or information content.
formal_slogan: If X is a random variable taking values in a countable additive group G, then the entropy of -X is the same as the entropy of X. This means reversing the sign of a symmetric random variable does not change its uncertainty. The result follows because negation is an injective operation in such groups.

informal_slogan: If a non-empty set A in a finite abelian group G with torsion m has a small sumset (A+A is at most K times the size of A), then A can be covered by at most m times K raised to the power 256m cubed plus one translates of a subgroup H, where H has size at most the size of A.
formal_slogan: If G is a finite abelian group where every element added to itself m times gives zero, and A is a non-empty subset of G such that the sumset A+A is not much larger than A (bounded by a factor K), then A can be covered by fewer than m times K raised to the power 256*m^3 + 1 translates of some subgroup H of G, where H has size at most the size of A.

informal_slogan: If A is a cocommutative bialgebra over a ring R, then the spectrum of A forms a commutative monoid scheme.
formal_slogan: If A is a commutative bialgebra over a commutative ring R and the coalgebra structure on A is cocommutative, then the spectrum of A as a scheme over the spectrum of R forms a commutative monoid object in the category of schemes over Spec(R).

informal_slogan: If a non-empty finite set A in the vector space F_2^n has a small sumset, meaning the size of A+A is at most K times the size of A, then A can be covered by at most 2K^9 copies of a subgroup H, where H has size at most the size of A.
formal_slogan: If a non-empty finite set A in a vector space over the field with two elements has a small sumset (the set of all pairwise sums of elements in A is at most K times larger than A), then A can be covered by at most 2K^9 translates of some subgroup H whose size is no larger than that of A.

informal_slogan: The image of the spectrum functor from R-algebras to schemes over Spec R consists exactly of those schemes that are affine over Spec R.
formal_slogan: The functor that sends R-algebras to their spectra gives exactly those schemes over Spec R which are affine; a scheme over Spec R is in the essential image of this functor if and only if it is affine.

informal_slogan: The entropy of the sum of independent random variables Y_j is at most the entropy of the sum of independent random variables X_i plus the sum over j of the difference between the entropy of (Y_j minus X_f(j)) and the entropy of X_f(j).
formal_slogan: If you have two sets of independent random variables X_i and Y_j, and each Y_j is paired with some X_f(j), then the entropy of the sum of the Y_j's is at most the entropy of the sum of the X_i's plus the sum of the entropies of the differences (Y_j - X_f(j)) minus the entropies of the corresponding X_f(j).

informal_slogan: For every dimension d, the highest possible density of sphere packings that repeat periodically in d-dimensional space is the same as the highest possible density of all sphere packings in that space, whether periodic or not.
formal_slogan: In any positive dimension d, the highest possible density of a periodic arrangement of non-overlapping spheres is the same as the highest density achievable by any arrangement, periodic or not. This means restricting to periodic patterns does not reduce the maximum packing density. The result equates two ways of measuring optimal sphere packing de…

informal_slogan: If x is a real number between -2 pi + eta and 2 pi - eta, with absolute value at least eta and eta positive, then the distance between 1 and the complex number e to the i x is at least 2 over pi times eta.
formal_slogan: For real numbers x and eta where eta is between 0 and pi, and the absolute value of x is at least eta and at most 2*pi - eta, the distance between 1 and the complex number exp(i*x) on the unit circle is at least (2/pi)*eta.

informal_slogan: If g is a bounded measurable periodic function bounded by a specific kernel k_r and f is another bounded measurable periodic function, then the L2 norm of their convolution h over one period is at most 17 times the L2 norm of f over the interval from -pi to pi.
formal_slogan: If f and g are bounded, periodic functions on the real line, and g is dominated by a nice kernel function scaled by r between 0 and pi, then the L2 norm of their convolution over one period is at most 17 times the L2 norm of f over the same interval.

informal_slogan: If a set A has a bounded internal covering number with constant c and exponent d, then every subset B of A also has a bounded internal covering number with constant 2 raised to the power d times c and the same exponent d.
formal_slogan: If a set A has a bounded covering number with constant c and exponent d, then any subset B of A also has a bounded covering number with constant (2^d * c) and the same exponent d, provided d is non-negative.

informal_slogan: If X, Y, and Z are random variables taking values in a group G, and the pair (X,Y) is independent of Z, then the entropy of the difference X minus Y is at most the sum of the entropies of X minus Z and Z minus Y, minus the entropy of Z.
formal_slogan: If X, Y, Z are independent random variables taking values in a countable abelian group, and each has only finitely many possible values, then the entropy of X - Y is at most the sum of the entropies of X - Z and Z - Y, minus the entropy of Z.

informal_slogan: If H is a finite subgroup of G and the rho value of U_H is at most r, then there is some shift t such that the intersection of A with the shifted subgroup H+t has size at least e^-r times the square root of |A| times |H|, and the ratio |H|/|A| is between e^-2r and e^2r.
formal_slogan: If H is a finite subgroup of G and the rho value of a uniform random variable over H is at most r, then there exists a shift t such that the intersection of set A with the shifted subgroup (H + t) has size at least e^(-r) times the square root of |A| times |H|, and the sizes of A and H are within a factor of e^(2r) of each other.

informal_slogan: For any point x and a finite set S in a space E, the distance from x to its nearest point in S is less than or equal to the distance from x to any other point in S.
formal_slogan: The distance from a point x to its nearest point in a finite set s is less than or equal to the distance from x to any point y in s.

informal_slogan: For a random variable X taking values in an additive group G, and a finite subgroup H of G, the entropy of the projection of X onto the quotient group G/H is at most twice the statistical distance between X and the uniform distribution on H.
formal_slogan: If X is a random variable taking values in an additive group G, and H is a finite subgroup of G, then the entropy of the projection of X onto the quotient group G/H is at most twice the Ruzsa distance between X and a random variable uniformly distributed on H.

informal_slogan: A pre-localizing sequence is a sequence of stopping times that almost surely increases to infinity as the index goes to infinity.
formal_slogan: A pre-localizing sequence is a sequence of stopping times, indexed by natural numbers, such that for almost every outcome, the values of the sequence eventually increase without bound, approaching infinity. informal_slogan: If X, Y, and Z are independent random variables taking values in a group G, then the Kullback-Leibler divergence between X+Z and Y+Z is less than or equal to the Kullback-Leibler divergence between X and Y.
formal_slogan: If X, Y, and Z are independent random variables taking values in a finite additive group, and Z is independent of the pair (X, Y), then the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the distributions of X + Z and Y + Z is less than or equal to the divergence between X and Y. informal_slogan: For a commutative ring R, there is a functor that sends each group G to the group algebra R[G], mapping from the category of groups to the category of Hopf algebras over R.
formal_slogan: commGrpAlg takes a commutative ring R and produces a functor that maps each commutative group to its group algebra over R, which naturally has the structure of a commutative Hopf algebra; this functor sends group homomorphisms to corresponding maps between Hopf algebras.

informal_slogan: The unit interval from 0 to 1 can be covered by at most 1/ε intervals of length 2ε when ε is less than or equal to 1.
formal_slogan: The smallest number of intervals of length 2ε needed to cover the interval from 0 to 1 is at most 1 divided by ε, when ε is between 0 and 1.

informal_slogan: The density of a sphere packing does not change when all the spheres are scaled by the same positive factor. Scaling the entire packing uniformly preserves how tightly the spheres are packed. This means the proportion of space filled by the spheres remains constant.
formal_slogan: Scaling a sphere packing in d-dimensional space by a positive factor does not change its density, because the proportion of space filled by the spheres remains the same even as all positions are uniformly scaled.

informal_slogan: If a representation of a finite group has trivial cohomology, then its Tate cohomology is also trivial.
formal_slogan: If a group representation has trivial cohomology, then its Tate cohomology is also trivial, provided the group is finite and the representation is over a commutative ring.

informal_slogan: In a finite abelian group where every element has order a power of 2, for any non-zero element x, exactly half of the homomorphisms from the group to the integers modulo 2 map x to 1.
formal_slogan: For a finite abelian group G where every element added to itself gives zero, and for any nonzero element x in G, the number of group homomorphisms from G to the integers mod 2 that send x to 1 is exactly half the size of G.

informal_slogan: A set is measurably analytic if it can be obtained as the projection of a measurable set from the product space of the original space and the real numbers. More generally, a set is measurably analytic for a space K if it is the projection of a measurable set from the product of the original space and K.

informal_slogan: A homotopy of formal solutions is a smoothly varying family of sections over time, where each section at any fixed time is a formal solution to a given relation.
formal_slogan: A homotopy of formal solutions is a continuous family of formal solutions parameterized by real numbers, where each solution satisfies a given differential relation between manifolds at every point in time.

informal_slogan: If two independent random variables X and Y are added together, the rho value of their sum is at most half the sum of their individual rho values plus half their dependence measure d[X;Y].
formal_slogan: If two random variables X and Y are independent, the rho value of their sum is at most the rho value of X plus half the difference between the entropy of their sum and the entropy of X.

informal_slogan: If a collection of functions is uniformly integrable, then the set of their conditional expectations with respect to any family of sigma-algebras is also uniformly integrable.
formal_slogan: If a family of functions is uniformly integrable with respect to a finite measure, then the family of their conditional expectations over a collection of sub-sigma-algebras is also uniformly integrable with respect to the same measure.

informal_slogan: A stochastic process is of class DL if it is progressively measurable and, for every fixed time t, the collection of its values at all stopping times up to t forms a uniformly integrable set.
formal_slogan: If a stochastic process is progressively measurable and, for each time t, the supremum of the norm of the process up to t is integrable, then the process is of class DL, meaning its stopped values up to any time form a uniformly integrable family.

informal_slogan: The periodic sphere packing constant in d dimensions is the highest possible density achieved by any periodic arrangement of non overlapping spheres in d dimensional space. It is found by taking the supremum of the density over all periodic packings in R d.
formal_slogan: The PeriodicSpherePackingConstant in dimension d is the least upper bound of the densities of all periodic sphere packings in that dimension, where density measures how much space the spheres fill. It is expressed as a value in the extended non-negative real numbers (ENNReal).

informal_slogan: A bialgebra is diagonalizable if it has the same structure as a group algebra. This means its elements and operations can be matched exactly with those of a group algebra. Diagonalizable bialgebras inherit properties from group algebras, such as commutativity or basis elements corresponding to group elements.
formal_slogan: A bialgebra is diagonalisable if it has the same structure as a group algebra over a commutative ring. This means there is a bijective correspondence between the bialgebra and a group algebra that preserves operations. The property depends on the base ring being commutative and the algebra having a compatible bialgebra structure.

formal_slogan: A set of real numbers is analytic with respect to the collection of all measurable sets if and only if it is analytic with respect to the collection of all closed intervals. informal_slogan: If X is a random variable taking values in a finite set S, then the entropy of X is less than or equal to the logarithm of the size of S.
formal_slogan: If a random variable X takes values in a finite set A almost surely, then its entropy is less than or equal to the natural logarithm of the number of elements in A.

formal_slogan: If X and Y are random variables taking values in the group of d-dimensional binary vectors, then there exists a subgroup H of this group such that the logarithm of the size of H is at most twice the sum of the entropies of X and Y, and the sum of the entropies of the projections of X and Y onto the quotient group G/H is at most 34 times the mutual…

informal_slogan: If a process is right continuous and you have a sequence of stopping times that approximate a given stopping time from above, then the values of the process at these approximating times converge almost surely to the value at the stopping time.
formal_slogan: For a right-continuous process X and a stopping time τ, if τn is a sequence of discrete approximations of τ that converges to τ from above almost surely, then the stopped values of X at τn converge almost surely to the stopped value of X at τ as n goes to infinity.

This quotient is well-defined due to the periodicity of Tate cohomology, which repeats every two degrees.

informal_slogan: The value of a Brownian motion at any positive time t follows a normal distribution with mean 0 and variance t.
formal_slogan: At any fixed time t, the value of a Brownian motion process has a normal distribution with mean 0 and variance t, under the given probability measure.

informal_slogan: A square integrable martingale is a càdlàg stochastic process indexed by a linearly ordered set with a filtration, such that the supremum of the L2 norms of its values over time is finite. This means the process is right-continuous with left limits and has uniformly bounded second moments.
formal_slogan: A square integrable martingale is a stochastic process indexed over a linearly ordered topological space, taking values in a complete normed real vector space, where the process is adapted to a filtration, has right-continuous paths with left limits (cadlag), and the expected value of the square of the process is uniformly bounded over time.

informal_slogan: If f is a group homomorphism and an open embedding between two locally compact topological groups, then pulling back a Haar measure on the target group along f gives a Haar measure on the source group.
formal_slogan: If a group homomorphism between two topological groups is an open embedding, then the pullback of a Haar measure on the target group through this map gives a Haar measure on the source group. informal_slogan: If a finite non-empty set A in the d-dimensional integers has small doubling in terms of U_A, then there is a relatively large subset A' of A, containing at least a K to the power of -17 fraction of A, and the dimension of A' is at most about 57 times the log of K.
formal_slogan: If a finite non-empty set A of integer lattice points in d dimensions has small doubling (measured by the log of K), then there is a non-empty subset A' of A that is at least K^(-17) times as large as A and lies in an affine subspace of dimension at most (40 / log 2) * log K.

informal_slogan: If a set in the product of a measurable space and the real numbers is analytic with respect to the product of the measurable sets and intervals, then its projection onto the measurable space is also analytic.
formal_slogan: If a set s in the product of a measurable space and the real numbers is measurable, then its projection onto the first component is analytic with respect to the paving of measurable sets.

informal_slogan: The group algebra functor, which sends a group G to its group algebra R[G] over a domain R, is fully faithful, meaning it preserves all structure and relationships between groups when mapping them into the category of Hopf algebras over R.
formal_slogan: The group algebra functor over a commutative ring R, when R is a domain, maps commutative groups and their homomorphisms to commutative Hopf algebras and their morphisms in a way that every homomorphism between group algebras comes from exactly one group homomorphism. This means the functor is fully faithful, preserving all structure between the c…

informal_slogan: If a family of sets includes the empty set and is closed under finite unions and intersections, and if a capacity is defined on this family, then every analytic set in this family can be approximated from within by sets in the family with respect to the capacity.
formal_slogan: If a collection of sets contains the empty set and is closed under finite intersections and finite unions, then any analytic set with respect to that collection can have its capacity approximated from above by sets in the collection.

informal_slogan: If a stopping time is bounded and approximated by a sequence of discrete stopping times, then the values of a martingale stopped at these discrete times form a uniformly integrable sequence.
formal_slogan: If X is a martingale and tau is a bounded stopping time, then the sequence of stopped values of X at a discrete approximation of tau is uniformly integrable with respect to the given finite measure.

informal_slogan: The dimension of the product of completions of L over the completions of K at infinite places equals the dimension of the tensor product of L with the completion of K at an infinite place, both considered as vector spaces over the completion of K.

informal_slogan: If M is a cadlag local martingale, then the square of its norm, ||M||^2, is a cadlag local submartingale.
formal_slogan: If a stochastic process is a local martingale and has right-continuous sample paths with left limits (cadlag), then the square of its norm is a local submartingale with respect to the same filtration and probability measure.

formal_slogan: The entropy of two random variables taken together does not depend on their order: the joint entropy of X and Y equals the joint entropy of Y and X. This holds when both variables are measurable and take values in countable spaces. Swapping the variables does not change the amount of uncertainty they represent together.

This means the optimal packing density can be found by only considering packings with unit separation distance. The result holds for all positive dimensions d.
